# Glossary

Abbreviations and slang you'll see in guides, group finder and chat.

Related: [[Status Effects]] · [[Perk Dictionary]] · [[Artifacts]] · [[New World Home]]

## Activities

| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **Expo / Expedition** | 5-player dungeon |
| **M1 / M2 / M3** | Mutated expedition difficulty 1–3 (M3 = Elite, 695 GS) |
| **Mutation / Mutator** | Weekly modifier on an expedition (Void, Fire, Nature or Ice element + buffs) |
| **OPR** | Outpost Rush (20v20 PvP) |
| **CTF** | Capture the Flag |
| **War** | 50v50 company territory siege |
| **Influence race** | Faction PvP missions that decide who can declare war |
| **ECR / Chest run** | Elite Chest Run: route of elite chests (e.g. Cutlass Keys, Nightbreak Roost) |
| **Raid** | 10-player content (Isle of Night, Hive of Gorgons) |
| **Catacombs** | Season 10 randomized 3-player dungeon |
| **Trial / Soul Trial** | Boss challenge activities |
| **Portal / Breach** | Corrupted portal / breach events in the open world |
| **Flagged** | PvP enabled in the open world |

## Gear and stats

| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **GS** | Gear score (cap 800 in S10) |
| **BiS** | Best in slot |
| **BoE / BoP** | Bind on Equip / Bind on Pickup |
| **Named** | Named item: fixed perks, can be upgraded at the Gypsum Kiln |
| **Artifact** | Unique orange-tier item with a special perk (see [[Artifacts]]) |
| **Infix** | S10 permanent artifact-strength perk on gear |
| **Charm** | S10 Perk Charm you socket into gear |
| **Umbrals** | Umbral Crystals: upgrade ≥700 GS gear to 800 |
| **Salt** | Azoth Salt: PvP Reward Track currency |
| **Gypsum** | Daily crafting material (Ruby, Garnet, Sapphire...) for kiln upgrades |
| **Light / Medium / Heavy** | Armor load: light = most damage + longest dodge; heavy = most defence + 15% more blocking + longer CC |
| **Str / Dex / Int / Foc / Con** | The five attributes |
| **Breakpoint** | Attribute threshold that unlocks a bonus (e.g. 300 Str = Grit on melee attacks) |
| **Magnify** | Artifact perk: + your highest attribute |
| **Runeglass** | Gem variant that adds elemental damage or special effects |
| **Attunement** | Weapon perk that adds an elemental hit (see [[Perk Dictionary]]) |

## Roles and builds

| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **DPS** | Damage dealer (also damage per second) |
| **Tank** | Holds aggro and soaks damage |
| **Healer** | Keeps the group alive (Life Staff) |
| **Bruiser** | Tanky melee damage dealer (often medium/heavy, e.g. Great Axe + War Hammer) |
| **Point tank** | Heavy PvP player who sits on capture points |
| **Diver / Assassin** | Player who jumps the enemy backline to kill healers and ranged |
| **Backline / Frontline** | Ranged/healers at the back / melee at the front |
| **Support mage** | Void/Ice Gauntlet player debuffing and CCing for the team |
| **Glass cannon** | High damage, low survivability |
| **Meta** | The strongest, most popular builds right now |

## Combat terms

| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **Aggro / Threat** | Who the enemy is targeting |
| **Taunt** | Force enemies onto you |
| **CC** | Crowd control (stun, root, slow, silence...) |
| **DoT** | Damage over time (bleed, burn, poison) |
| **AoE** | Area of effect |
| **Proc** | When a perk or effect triggers |
| **Cooldown (CD)** | Time until an ability can be used again |
| **CDR** | Cooldown reduction (Refreshing perks) |
| **i-frames** | Invulnerability frames during a dodge |
| **Kiting** | Moving away while attacking so enemies can't hit you |
| **Animation cancel** | Starting one action to cut short another (e.g. Berserk into Feral Rush) |
| **Light / Heavy attack** | Tap vs hold attack |
| **Weapon swap** | Switching between your two weapons |
| **Backstab** | Hit from behind (bonus damage) |
| **Headshot** | Bow/musket hit to the head (bonus damage) |
| **Execute** | Ability or bonus that finishes low-health targets |
| **Stack / Stacks** | Group up in one spot / number of times a buff or debuff is applied |
| **Burst** | Big damage in a short window |
| **Peel** | Protect a teammate by CCing whoever's attacking them |
| **One-shot** | Kill in a single hit |
| **Enrage / Soft enrage** | Boss gets stronger the longer the fight lasts |
| **Downed** | Knocked to the ground and needing a revive (once per expedition run before respawn) |

## Chat shorthand

| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **LFG / LFM** | Looking for group / looking for more |
| **WTB / WTS / WTT** | Want to buy / sell / trade |
| **TP** | Trading post |
| **GG / GJ** | Good game / good job |
| **OOM** | Out of mana |
| **AFK / BRB** | Away / be right back |
| **Inv** | Invite me to your group |

# Status Effects

What the buffs, debuffs and combat terms in your notes mean, with **Season 10 values** from MrMojitoTV's Empower/Fortify/Debuffs sheet.

Related: [[Perk Dictionary]] · [[Glossary]] · [[Artifacts]] · [[Gems]] · [[New World Home]]

> [!note] Values are for 700 GS perks; "II" = the 800 GS version. Durations and cooldowns are in seconds (the sheet doesn't label those columns, so treat them as likely, not certain). Sheet version 10.0.0 (28 Oct 2025) for game version 10.0.2.

## Caps (Season 10)

| Effect | Cap | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| **Empower** | +50% | Weaken subtracts from it (Empower − Weaken) |
| **Weaken** | −50% | – |
| **Fortify** | +200% physical, +200% elemental | "Special" fortify perks cap at 50% |
| **Rend** | −70% physical / −70% elemental armor; −30% absorption | Scales with the target's armor |

## Crowd control (CC)

| Effect | What it does | Tip |
|---|---|---|
| **Stun** | Can't do anything | Best way to interrupt a Grit attack |
| **Root** | Can't move, but can still attack and use abilities | Social Distancing / Berserk escape it |
| **Silence** | Can't use abilities, basic attacks still work | – |
| **Stagger** | Interrupts the current action (beaten by Grit) | Heavy attacks stagger Behemoths in The Depths |
| **Knockdown / Flatten** | Puts the target on the ground; Flatten is War Hammer's version | Wrecking Ball, Sweep |
| **Knockback / Pull** | Pushes away / drags in | Shield Rush, Reap, Gravity Well |
| **Taunt** | Forces enemies to attack you | Carnelian gem + Shield Bash, Shockwave, Defender's Resolve |

**Freedom** perks make Slow, Stun and Silence wear off faster. **Djinn Headwrap** shortens non-CC debuffs.

## Damage over time (DoTs)

| Effect | Damage type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| **Bleed** | Physical | Keenly Jagged, Rapier, The Butcher |
| **Burn** | Fire | Fire Staff; lava in Empyrean Forge stacks it |
| **Poison** | Elemental | Spear (Venom), Aconite, Pestilence |
| **Shock** | Stamina | Drains stamina over time |
| **Disintegrate** | Weapon | Damage over time **and** Rend (10% per stack, counts toward the Rend cap) |
| **Frostbite / Chill** | Ice | 50% Slow + 10% Rend; Deep Freeze does +15% vs chilled/frozen/rooted |
| **Blight** | – | Garden of Genesis water: cuts healing + DoT |

## Other mechanics

| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **Exhausted (state)** | Your stamina hit zero: you can't dodge or sprint until it recovers (different from the Exhaust debuff) |
| **Debuff Resilience** | M2/M3 expedition bosses take Rend 50% less effective and Weaken 75% less effective (caps unchanged) |
| **Non-dispellable** | Buffs/debuffs marked this way can't be cleansed (e.g. Baleful Tether, food buffs) |
| **Threat / aggro** | How much enemies want to attack you; tanks raise it, DPS/healers lower it (Beloved, Calming) |

## Damage formula (from the sheet)

Damage = Weapon damage × ability modifier × (1 + base damage bonuses + crit) × **(1 + Empower − Weaken)** × (1 + enemy-type bonus) × (1 − armor mitigation × (1 − armor penetration)) × (1 − absorption)

Armor mitigation goes up with **Fortify** and down with **Rend**, which is why tanks stack Fortify and DPS stack Rend.

# Winter Convergence

The winter event's own items: what each one is, how you get it and what it turns into.⁠​‌‌​​​​​​‌​‌‌‌​‌‌‌‌‌‌​​‌⁠ Winter Tokens are spent in the Winter Village.

Related: [[Game Modes]] · [[Where to gather]] · [[New World Home]]

> [!info] Taken from the game data NW Buddy ships for Season 10. The event only runs in winter, so these items only drop while it's live.

## Event items

| Item | Type | How you get it | What it's for |
|---|---|---|---|
| Gleamite | Resource | Gathered from Gleamite shards and chunks that appear during the event | Turn it into Winter Tokens at a Holiday Hut in the Winter Village |
| Recovered Present | Resource | Picked up from Lost Presents, about 2,000 spots across every zone (most in Brimstone Sands, Cutlass Keys, Monarch's Bluffs, Brightwood and Edengrove) | Turn it into Winter Tokens at a Holiday Hut in the Winter Village |
| Hastily Wrapped Present | Container | Event reward addressed to you | Opens into Winter Tokens, with a chance of a Lockbox |
| Beautifully Wrapped Present | Container | Event reward addressed to you | Opens into Winter Tokens and Premium Winter Tokens, with a chance of a Lockbox |
| Exquisitely Wrapped Present | Container | Event reward addressed to you | Opens into Winter Tokens and Premium Winter Tokens, with a chance of a Lockbox |

## Quick tips

| Tip | Why |
|---|---|
| Pick up every Lost Present you pass | Recovered Presents are spread over the whole map, so they add up while you travel |
| Cash in at a Holiday Hut | Both Gleamite and Recovered Presents only become Winter Tokens there |
| Save the fancier presents | Beautifully and Exquisitely Wrapped Presents are the ones that can give Premium Winter Tokens |

# Drop Limits

All 338 loot limits in the game data: how many of something you can get, and how often the limit resets.

Related: [[Gear Grind]] · [[Gear Score to 800]] · [[Expeditions Overview]] · [[Consumables]]

> [!note] **Count** is how many times it can drop before the limit is hit. **Resets** is how long the limit window lasts. The game's "daily" window is 18 hours, which works out to the daily server reset. **Gap** is the shortest time between two drops, when the data sets one. Some limits are older or event-only and may not be active right now.

# Weapon Scaling

Base numbers for every weapon at tier 5: base damage, crit, stagger, attribute scaling and blocking.

Related: [[Attribute Breakpoints]] · [[Skill Trees]] · [[Gear Basics]] · [[Set Pieces]]

> [!note] **Scaling** is how much each attribute point adds to the weapon's damage, from the weapon's own data. The bigger number is the weapon's main attribute; the smaller one still adds damage. A weapon item can override these, but almost none do. Gear score and perks are applied on top of the base damage.

## Weapons

| Weapon | Base damage | Crit chance | Crit damage | Stagger damage | Main stat | Scaling per point |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Sword | 64 | 7% | ×1.3 | 36 | STR | STR 0.85% / DEX 0.65% |
| Flail | 64 | 6% | ×1.2 | 39 | STR | STR 0.85% / FOC 0.65% |
| Rapier | 61 | 9% | ×1.4 | 28 | DEX | DEX 0.85% / INT 0.65% |
| Hatchet | 67 | 8% | ×1.4 | 30 | STR | STR 0.75% / DEX 0.75% |
| Dagger | 60 | 7% | ×1.3 | 36 | DEX | DEX 0.95% / STR 0.4% |
| Great Axe | 89 | 7% | ×1.35 | 60 | STR | STR 0.95% / INT 0.4% |
| Greatsword | 77 | 7% | ×1.25 | 60 | STR | STR 0.75% / DEX 0.75% |
| War Hammer | 93 | 6% | ×1.2 | 64 | STR | STR 0.95% / DEX 0.4% |
| Spear | 70 | 9% | ×1.3 | 46 | DEX | DEX 0.85% / STR 0.65% |
| Bow | 84 | 8% | ×1.3 | 38 | DEX | DEX 0.95% / STR 0.4% |
| Musket | 98 | 7% | ×1.3 | 54 | DEX | DEX 0.85% / INT 0.65% |
| Blunderbuss | 93 | 6% | ×1.15 | 54 | STR | STR 0.85% / INT 0.65% |
| Fire Staff | 65 | 10% | ×1.25 | 34 | INT | INT 0.95% / DEX 0.4% |
| Life Staff | 55 | 6% | ×1.2 | 32 | FOC | FOC 0.95% / INT 0.4% |
| Ice Gauntlet | 67 | 9% | ×1.3 | 43 | INT | INT 0.95% / STR 0.4% |
| Void Gauntlet | 64 | 8% | ×1.3 | 41 | INT | INT 0.85% / FOC 0.65% |

## Shields

Shield base damage is used for shield bash attacks; block stability matters more for tanking.

| Shield | Base damage | Crit chance | Crit damage | Stagger damage | Main stat | Scaling per point |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Round Shield | 63 | 7% | ×1.3 | 54 | STR | STR 0.85% / DEX 0.65% |
| Kite Shield | 60 | 7% | ×1.3 | 48 | STR | STR 0.85% / DEX 0.65% |
| Tower Shield | 56 | 7% | ×1.3 | 42 | STR | STR 0.85% / DEX 0.65% |

## Blocking

**Block stamina damage** is the stamina the weapon's hits drain from an enemy's block. **Block stability** is how well the weapon holds a block: higher means less of your own stamina is lost. Tower Shield is highest.

| Weapon | Block stamina damage | Block stability | Can block ranged |
|---|---|---|---|
| Sword | 36 | 22 | yes |
| Flail | 39 | 24 | yes |
| Rapier | 28 | 17 | yes |
| Hatchet | 30 | 21 | yes |
| Dagger | 36 | 15 | yes |
| Great Axe | 60 | 27 | yes |
| Greatsword | 60 | 34 | yes |
| War Hammer | 64 | 27 | yes |
| Spear | 46 | 25 | yes |
| Bow | 38 | 0 | – |
| Musket | 54 | 0 | – |
| Blunderbuss | 54 | 0 | – |
| Fire Staff | 34 | 17 | yes |
| Life Staff | 32 | 22 | yes |
| Ice Gauntlet | 43 | 30 | yes |
| Void Gauntlet | 41 | 22 | yes |
| Round Shield | 54 | 30 | yes |
| Kite Shield | 48 | 40 | yes |
| Tower Shield | 42 | 50 | yes |

## What this means for each role

| Role | Takeaway |
|---|---|
| Tank | Sword, War Hammer and Great Axe all scale mainly with Strength, so they pair with a Strength + Constitution build. Tower Shield has the best block stability; Round Shield the lowest. |
| Bruiser | War Hammer has the highest melee base and stagger damage, good for breaking blocks. Flail is Strength with Focus for off-tank support. |
| Melee DPS | Rapier and Spear scale mainly with Dexterity; Rapier and Hatchet crits hit hardest (x1.4). |
| Ranged DPS | Bow and Musket are Dexterity weapons; Musket has the highest ranged base damage. Blunderbuss is Strength with Intelligence. |
| Mage | Fire Staff and Ice Gauntlet scale mainly with Intelligence; Fire Staff has the highest base crit chance (10%). |
| Healer | Life Staff scales with Focus, with a little Intelligence. |

# Artifacts

All 72 artifacts in the Season 10 game data: their unique perk, what it does, where it drops, and which build uses it.⁠​‌‌​​​​​​‌​‌‌‌​‌‌‌‌‌‌​​‌⁠ Bold ones are used in a build on this site.

Related: [[Perk Dictionary]] · [[Status Effects]] · [[Gear Grind]] · [[New World Home]]

## How artifacts work

| Thing | Detail |
|---|---|
| Perks | Six perks: a **unique perk**, **Magnify** (+ your highest attribute; it's a stat, not an artifact), a gem socket and others |
| Unlocking | Each perk is unlocked through the artifact's own quest |
| 5th perk | Upgrade at a Gypsum Kiln to add a perk of your choice |
| Season 10 | Can be upgraded to 800 GS with Umbral Crystals like other ≥700 gear |
| PvP track artifacts | Bought with Azoth Salt; buying ones you don't want removes them from the pool |

# Heart Runes

Your ultimate ability, in the slot under your weapons.⁠​‌‌​​​​​​‌​‌‌‌​‌‌‌‌‌‌​​‌⁠ Also called heart gems (the game data calls the item class `HeartGem` and the ability a Heartrune).

Related: [[Perk Dictionary]] · [[Perk Charms]] · [[Status Effects]] · [[Gems]] · [[Skill Trees]] · [[Attribute Breakpoints]] · [[Glossary]] · [[New World Home]]

> [!note] Effects below are cross-checked against the game data you gave me. One difference: the guide says Accelerating Storm gives +15% movement speed, the data says **12%** — the data is what I've used.

## How they work

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| Slot | Under your weapons. Swap it like any other gear |
| Charging | Light attacks, heavy attacks and abilities fill the meter. **Taking damage does not** |
| Using it | Press **G** when full. The meter empties |
| Cooldown | None. You just have to refill the meter |

## Tiers

| Tier | How you get it |
|---|---|
| Minor | Drops from an expedition boss, or craft with dense expedition materia (8,000; Bile Bomb is 5,000 Mutator Materia) |
| Major | Stonecutting station, from the Minor rune + 5 Wooden Coin, 5 Gypsum Orb, 5 Corrupted Lodestone, 3 Sulfur |
| Legendary (625) | Three versions. **Cunning** = 50 Vial of Suspended Azoth · **Stalwart** = 5 Writ of Adventure · **Brutal** = 5 Corrupted Lodestone. All three also need 10 Wooden Coin, 10 Gypsum Orb, 10 Sulfur |
| 700 | The 625 version + 50 Gypsum Orb, 10 Runic Voidstone, 50 Vial of Suspended Azoth |

You keep the Minor rune: it's the crafting artifact for the Major version.

## Variants

All three legendary versions share the same first perk. Only the **second** perk differs, and that's what the Cunning / Stalwart / Brutal name means. There's no fixed rule to it, so read the rune: on Stoneform, Stalwart is the heal and Brutal is an explosion, but on Cannon Blast, Stalwart is the knockdown.

## The ten heart runes

| Rune | Base effect | Shared perk |
|---|---|---|
| **Stoneform** | Cleanses CC debuffs, and gives stagger + CC immunity for 4s | Fortifying Form: +10% armor for 4s on activation |
| **Detonate** | Charge for 3s, then explode for 100% in 5m | Accelerating Charge: +20% movement speed while charging |
| **Grasping Vines** | 100% damage, roots everything within 4m for 3s | Enfeebling Vines: Weaken, −20% their damage for 8s |
| **Dark Ascent** | Fly up (brief invulnerability), then slam for 100% + stagger in 3m. Press again to drop early | Leeching Ascent: heal 100% of the damage dealt |
| **Cannon Blast** | Summons a cannon for a long-range 100% shot. Has Grit | Burning Blast: Burn for 10% rune damage/s for 5s |
| **Fire Storm** | A 2m fire tornado travels 17m: 100% damage + Burn (30%/s for 6s). Allies inside get 10% Empower for 6s | Enfeebling Storm: Weaken, −15% damage for 8s |
| **Bile Bomb** | A 3.5m cloud for 3s: 100%/s, and −30% incoming / −15% outgoing healing for 8s. A direct hit makes the cloud stick to them | Crippling Bile: Slow, −20% movement speed for 3s |
| **Phantom Blades** | Blades spin for 7s, hitting for 100% every 0.7s within 4m | Merciless Incision: +20% damage to targets under Stun, Root, Slow or Sluggish |
| **The Devourer** | Summon up to 15m away for 40% + knockdown in 2.5m; the chomp does 100% in 2m | Crippling Dispersal: 20% Slow for 5s on the first hit |
| **Primal Fury** | Enrage: stagger + 150% in 3m, then beast form for 10s (light 100%, heavy leap 120% + knockdown). Press again to end it for 150% in 3m. Needs Rise of the Angry Earth | Lasting Rage: +10s duration |

## Second perk by variant

| Rune | Cunning | Stalwart | Brutal |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Stoneform** | Hardened Form: +10% armor per hit taken for 4s (max +30%) | Mending Form: heal 52% rune damage/s while active, −20% your damage | Unstable Form: explodes for 200% in 3m when it ends or on a second press, 2s shorter |
| **Detonate** | Empowering Charge: +15% your damage while charging, −20% explosion damage | Leeching Explosion: heal 50% of explosion damage, −30% explosion damage | Escalating Explosion: +20% explosion damage, but Rend yourself −50% armor while charging |
| **Grasping Vines** | Leeching Vines: heal 20% of damage done to rooted targets | Resilient Vines: +20% armor on activation, −20% your damage for 5s | Rending Vines: Rend −20% their armor for 5s, −50% your stamina regen for 5s |
| **Dark Ascent** | Crippling Ascent: Slow −30% movement for 4s | Fortifying Ascent: +10% armor per hit (max 3), −10% your damage for 5s per hit | Empowered Ascent: hits deal 150%, but no stagger |
| **Cannon Blast** | Penetrating Blast: passes through enemies, can't be blocked | Concussive Blast: knocks down, but only 30% damage | Explosive Blast: explodes in 3m, −20% damage |
| **Fire Storm** | Accelerating Storm: allies get Haste, +12% movement speed for 8s | Cleansing Storm: cleanses damage-over-time from allies it passes through, −15% Burn damage | Expedited Storm: travels faster, 200% damage, no Burn |
| **Bile Bomb** | Exhausting Bile: Exhaust, −30% their stamina regen | Mending Bile: anyone hitting the afflicted heals 20% of their damage; healing cut drops to 15%/7.5%, no damage over time | Concentrated Bile: healing cut rises to 50%/25% and damage to 150%/s, but no cloud on impact |
| **Phantom Blades** | Achilles' Heel: blades creep forward and apply Sluggish (no dodging) for 2s or until they hit. Can't reapply within 10s | Freeing Blades: each hit cuts your own CC durations by 10% | Mobile Destruction: blades follow you, radius 2.5m, damage 70% |
| **The Devourer** | Infected Chomp: poison for 15% rune damage/s for 7s | Devourer's Fury: Uninterruptible for 5s after it damages something, but Weaken −20% your damage while active | Emerging Convergence: first hit does 200% and pulls targets in, no knockdown |
| **Primal Fury** | Unstoppable Rage: Grit in beast form | Extending Coat: +20% Fortify, −15% Weaken; taking damage extends it up to 10s | Extending Claws: +20% Empower, −15% Rend; dealing damage extends it up to 10s |

## Which one to run

| You're playing | Pick | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Point tank / war frontline | **Stalwart Stoneform** | Breaks the CC chain, gives armor and a heal while you hold the circle. The default tank pick |
| Solo tank in the open world | **Stalwart Stoneform** | Called "a must" in the solo guides: it's your panic button and your self-heal |
| Dive bruiser | **Brutal Detonate** | The most damage into a clump. Play safe for a while after you use it |
| Safer bruiser | **Cunning Detonate** | Same idea, less risk |
| Any build that keeps dying to stuns | **Cunning Stoneform** | The most defensive option in the game |
| Group pull setup | **Brutal Grasping Vines** | Clumps them and Rends, so your Great Axe or Hammer follows up harder |
| Fire Staff / mage | **Stalwart Dark Ascent** | Invulnerable attack that heals you out of trouble |
| Healer | **Stalwart Stoneform** | Fortify plus a heal over time; Minor Stoneform is the most defensive |
| Open-world roaming | **Cunning Phantom Blades** | Sustained AoE that follows the fight |

| Purifying Heart | Ring | Lose all debuffs on heartrune |

## Attunements

**What they are:** a weapon perk that adds a burst of **elemental damage** on top of your normal hits. Example: Frost Attunement makes attacks deal an extra 15% weapon damage as Ice, with a 2-second cooldown. It doesn't trigger off damage-over-time effects. Older "Attunement II" versions are the fixed/upgraded tier.

| Attunement | Element | Good against (mobs) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Flame Attunement | Fire | Angry Earth | Most PvP players resist Fire, so avoid it in PvP |
| Frost Attunement | Ice | Lost, Ice-weak bosses (Ifrit, Marius, Nereid) | Most PvP players resist Ice, so avoid it in PvP |
| Shock Attunement | Lightning | Ancient (+30%) | Good PvE vs Ancients |
| Arboreal Attunement | Nature | Lost (+30%), Corrupted | Scales with Focus |
| Abyssal Attunement | Void | Ancient | Scales with Int |
| Arcane Attunement | Arcane | Corrupted (+30%), Ifrit | Common PvP pick |

### How to use them

| Rule | Why |
|---|---|
| Match your **weapon gem / runeglass element** to the Attunement | Both deal the same element, so the damage stacks |
| Add the matching **ring damage perk** (e.g. Arcane Damage) | +3% of that element boosts gem, Attunement and DoT damage |
| PvE: pick the element the enemy is weak to | See [[1 Bosses]] for exact % |
| PvP: avoid Fire and Ice | Most players carry resistance to them |

### Attunement vs Conversion vs Chain

| Perk type | What it does | Example |
|---|---|---|
| **Attunement** | Extra elemental hit on attacks (cooldown) | Frost Attunement: +15% weapon damage as Ice |
| **Conversion** | Converts 20–50% of your damage into an element (scales off weapon stat or Int; Focus for Arboreal) | Abyssal (Void), Arboreal (Nature), Electrified (Lightning), Empowered (Arcane), Ignited (Fire), Frozen (Ice) |
| **Chain** | On hit, an elemental chain bounces between nearby enemies | Chain Lightning, Chain Fire, Chain Void, Chain Ice, Chain Nature |
| **Shirking (element)** | Dodging through an attack makes your next hit deal extra elemental damage | Shirking Nature: next hit within 5 s deals +19% base weapon damage as Nature |

# Housing

What a house gives you, what each house tier costs, and how trophies work.⁠​‌‌​​​​​​‌​‌‌‌​‌‌‌‌‌‌​​‌⁠ Every trophy and how to get it: [[Trophies]].

Related: [[Trophies]] · [[Tradeskills]] · [[Crafting Stations]] · [[Gear Grind]]

## Why own a house

| Benefit | Detail |
|---|---|
| Trophies | Up to 5 buff trophies per house: more damage against an enemy type, better crafted gear score, more gathering yield |
| Fast travel | Recall to your house for free on a cooldown (shorter for bigger houses) |
| Storage | Placed storage chests add extra storage in that town |
| Furniture | Place furniture for looks and house ranking points |

## House tiers

> [!note] Costs are the base price from the game data. The town's property tax and upkeep come on top. **Standing** is the territory standing level you need in that town.

| House | Base cost | Standing needed | Max items | Trophies | Storage chests | Recall cooldown |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Tier 1 | 5,000 gold | 1 | 100 | 5 | 1 | 4 h |
| Tier 2 | 10,000 gold | 1 | 125 | 5 | 2 | 3 h |
| Tier 3 | 15,000 gold | 20 | 150 | 5 | 3 | 150 min |
| Tier 4 | 20,000 gold | 30 | 200 | 5 | 4 | 2 h |
| Tier 5 (special) | 90,000 gold | 50 | 250 | 0 | 0 | 2 h |

## How trophies work

| Rule | Detail |
|---|---|
| Five per house | Each house holds up to 5 trophies |
| One of each kind | Two Beast combat trophies in the same house don't stack |
| Three steps | Minor → Basic → Major. Making the next one uses up the one before |
| Made at a Workshop | Furnishing tradeskill at a Workshop (Engineering station). Minor needs level 75; Major needs 200 |
| Combat trophies | +% damage against one enemy type (Ancient, Angry Earth, Beast, Corrupted, Lost, Human). Pair them with your coatings: see [[Consumables]] |

# Gear Grind

Where to farm the best gear in Season 10 (Nighthaven). Season 10 runs until the servers close on **31 Jan 2027**.

| Note | What's in it |
|---|---|
| [[PvP Gear Tier List]] | Which PvP modes give the best PvP gear, plus what you need for each |
| [[PvE Gear Tier List]] | Which raids, Catacombs and expeditions give the best PvE gear, plus what you need for each |
| [[Gear Score to 800]] | How to get from 700 to 800 with Umbral Crystals, and what each step costs |
| [[Gear Basics]] | Which artifacts, perks and sets each role (tank, bruiser, melee, ranged, mage, healer) wants |
| [[Drop Limits]] | Daily and weekly caps: gypsum, group finder rewards, trials, world bosses |
| [[1 Raids]] | Isle of Night, Hive of Gorgons and Sandworm, boss by boss |

## Quick facts

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| Max level / gear score | 70 / 800 |
| PvP scaling | OPR, Arena etc. scale everyone to 775 (Wars do **not**: gear score matters there) |
| Gear sets | Only from Isle of Night raid, Catacombs and the PvP Reward Track |
| Upgrading | Any gear ≥700 GS can be upgraded to 800 with Umbral Crystals |

## Gear sets and where they come from

> [!tip] These summaries are checked against the game data. Full tooltip text for every perk is in [[Gear Sets]].

> [!note] **Every set comes in every slot.** The item data has 33 pieces per set (Thaumaturge's has 21): all five armour slots in light, medium and heavy, plus amulet, ring, earring and weapons. Every piece and its fixed perks: [[Set Pieces]].

| Set | Source | In-game item names | Pieces needed | What it actually does | Best for |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Dreadwarden's (Second Wind) | Isle of Night raid | **Dreadwarden's …** | 2 / 4 | **Only works while exhausted.** +20% base damage to enemies within 5m, and hitting one removes the dodge-exhaustion slow. Second perk: 10% lifesteal while exhausted, plus 3% Empower stacks (max 5) when you come out of it | Bruiser, PvP tank |
| Spectral Wrath (Enrage) | Isle of Night raid | **Spectral Wrath …** | 1 / 3 / 5 | Hits within 13m stack Enrage: +1% damage but **+0.5% damage taken** per stack. Perk 2 raises the cap to 15 and heavy attacks add stacks, but **you lose 5% max HP every half second while above 70% health**. Perk 3: cap 25, +50% duration, +8% damage below 70% health | Melee and ranged DPS |
| Hallowed Aegis (Protector's Blessing) | Isle of Night raid | **Hallowed Aegis …** | 2 / 4 | Healing an ally above 50% health stacks Protector's Blessing. At 5 stacks you take 7% Rend, but healing an above-50% ally gives them 15% fortification. Perk 2: +3% base damage per stack; at max, healing someone below 50% consumes the stacks to heal them 10% weapon damage per second for 5s | Healer |
| Overcharged | Catacombs | **Barrow Robber's / Plunderer's …** | 3 / 5 | Hits or kills within 5m stack: +5% base damage and +10% affliction resistance each, but **+4% Rend per stack**. Getting hit wipes all stacks (max 3). Perk 2: max 5 stacks, and each adds 5% stamina regen | Melee DPS (burst, PvE) |
| Elementally Charged | Catacombs | **Grave Offering …** | 2 / 4 | Magic abilities deal **7% less** base damage but store that element for 20s; a non-magic ability then consumes it to add 10% weapon damage as that element for 10s. Perk 2: 2 charges per element, and 10% resistance to that element at 2 | Mage, hybrid weapons |
| Tenacity | PvP Reward Track (by elimination) | **Insurmountable …** | 2 / 4 | Grit for 2s after being staggered, but **+5% damage taken while grit is active**. Perk 2: light attacks give Grit for 3s (6s cooldown) and 5% lifesteal while it's up | Tank, bruiser |
| Stifling | PvP Reward Track (by elimination) | **Obstructor's …** | 2 / 4 | Hitting with all your abilities on cooldown silences the target 2s and you 1s (once per 5s). Perk 2: +10% basic attack damage while silenced, and hits cut ability cooldowns 5% | PvP damage, chasers |
| Focused | PvP Reward Track (by elimination) | **Thaumaturge's …** | 2 / 4 | +15% healing on targets standing outside Sacred Ground or Beacon. Perk 2: +15% healing and 5% cooldown reduction after holding the weapon 10s | Healer |

\*The three PvP sets are still worked out by elimination: there are 8 sets, the raid and Catacombs ones are confirmed by guides, and the game data records the bonuses but not where the gear drops.⁠​‌‌​​​​​​‌​‌‌‌​‌‌‌‌‌‌​​‌⁠ Check in-game.

> [!tip] **Read the conditions before you farm a set.** Second Wind only works while you're **exhausted** (out of stamina), so it suits bruisers who dodge and swing until empty, not tanks who block. Overcharged loses its stacks whenever you're hit, so it's for burst damage dealers. Spectral Wrath makes you take more damage the more stacks you build. Which set each role should chase: [[Gear Basics]].

# Gear Score to 800

| Step | Gear score | How |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | ~640–650 | Main story |
| 2 | 650 → 685 | Base expeditions (gear capped at 685) |
| 3 | 685 → 700 | Mutations (M1 650 / M2 675 / M3 695 GS), named mobs/chests in top zones, corrupted portals |
| 4 | 700 → 750 | Catacombs Sterling caches (750 GS), crafting with Prismatic Scarab (guaranteed 700 + chosen perks, weekly cooldown) |
| 5 | 700+ → 800 | **Umbral Crystals.** Any gear ≥700 can be upgraded. Isle of Night drops up to 800 directly |

## Umbral Crystals

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| Weekly cap | Raised to **100,000** per week (April 2026) |
| Drop rate | **Tripled** (June 2026 update) |
| Sources | Quests, mutations, PvP Reward Track + PvP modes, raids, Catacombs, invasion caches, war caches, elite chests, stockpiles |
| How to apply | Right-click the gear → Attach Charm |
| Rough pace | ~5 pieces per week from 730 to 800 (older estimate, before the cap and drop-rate boosts) |

## What each step costs (game data)

The upgrade cost per gear score point, from `GearScoreUpgrade` in your game export.⁠​‌‌​​​​​​‌​‌‌‌​‌‌‌‌‌‌​​‌⁠ The numbers are in the game's own units, so compare them rather than reading them as crystals.

| Upgrade | Cost per point | Total for the step | Share of 700 → 800 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 700 → 785 | 5 | 425 | 46% |
| 785 → 790 | 7, 10, 12, 15, 20 | 64 | 7% |
| 790 → 800 | 24 rising to 70 | 437 | 47% |
| **700 → 800** | | **926** | 100% |

> [!tip] The **last 10 points cost about as much as the first 85**. Get every piece to 790 before taking any to 800, and finish with the pieces that matter most (weapons first). Daily gypsum and other caps: [[Drop Limits]].

# PvE Gear Tier List

Best places to grind **PvE gear**, ranked.⁠​‌‌​​​​​​‌​‌‌‌​‌‌‌‌‌‌​​‌⁠ The tiers are my own ranking based on what each activity rewards in Season 10 guides.

## Tier list

| Tier | Activity | Why it's here | What you get |
|---|---|---|---|
| **S** | Isle of Night raid (10-man) | Hardest content, best loot. ~100 items, 3 sets | Gear up to 800; Spectral Wrath, Dreadwarden's, Hallowed Aegis sets (light/medium/heavy); tokens, Chromatic Seals, Relic Shards |
| **S** | Catacombs (3-man) | Easiest way to get set pieces | Sterlings → 750 GS caches; Crowns → Overcharged / Elementally Charged set pieces; perk charm mats; cosmetics |
| **A** | Mutated expeditions – M3 (Elite) | Best expedition tier for gear + artifacts; Umbral source | High-GS gear, artifacts, Umbrals. Weekly limit raised to 100 runs (May 2026) |
| **B** | Nighthaven bosses / elite chests | Fast legendaries for quick GS upgrades in a raid group | Guaranteed legendary from bosses, Umbrals from elite chests |
| **B** | Hive of Gorgons raid | Old 725 sets, but anything ≥700 can now be pushed to 800 | 725 Hoplite / Gorgon gear, 10 tokens per clear, Gorgon's Eye (crafting) |
| **B** | Mutated expeditions – M1/M2 | Stepping stones to M3 | Gear (higher tier = higher minimum drops), Umbrals |
| **C** | Base expeditions, open world, corrupted portals | Catch-up only | Up to 685 (expeditions) / 700 (named, chests, portal caches) |

## What you need for each

| Activity | Level | Group | Gear score | Other requirements / prep |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Isle of Night | 70 | 6–10 (raid group, Group Finder) | Near 800, at least mid-700s. Whole group is blocked if anyone is under the minimum | Lost Ward Potions, Lost Coatings, Fire Absorption Food. Prioritise Strike + Nature damage. Max your mitigation/ward/resist perks |
| Catacombs | 70 (recommended) | Up to 3 (Activity Finder) | Not specified | 30-min timer; only one player needs to exit for everyone to keep loot. Tank + healer + DPS. Vendor: Rikkar, Inn at Nighthaven |
| M3 Elite mutation | 70 | 5 | 695 | Usual expedition comp (tank, healer, 3 DPS) |
| M2 Hard mutation | 70 | 5 | 675 | – |
| M1 Intermediate mutation | 70 | 5 | 650 | Unlocks after base expeditions (reach 685 GS) |
| Nighthaven bosses / elite chests | 70 | Raid group recommended | – | Group up and farm the worthwhile bosses |
| Hive of Gorgons | Endgame | 10 | ~725 era | Gorgonite schematic or Inductor + Aquae Rejya to craft from Gorgon's Eye |

## Isle of Night bosses

Full boss-by-boss notes and debuffs: [[Isle of Night]].

| # | Boss | Watch out for |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Twin Jesters | Bombs (kill them before they reach the group), fire rings, clones; final phase is a timed DPS check with reduced healing |
| 2 | Dahut, Ys Heiress + Palatine Guards | Guards revive; fire marks and moving fire rings |
| 3 | Overlord Thorpe | Stun him while he summons the Spear; adds at 70% HP; ground fissures |

## Catacombs tips

| Tip | Detail |
|---|---|
| Crowns | Only from the **2nd boss onward**, so push past boss 1 |
| Idol of Ascension | Spend Splintered Souls (100) there; they can't be taken out of the run |
| Aspects (buffs) | Only one player can take each. Defensive ones go to whoever is taking hits, damage ones to the damage dealers |
| Corruption | Use Golden Tinctures from small chests when the meter is high |
| Exit | Leave time to get out. A failed run loses most of your loot |

## Route for every role

| Step | Do this |
|---|---|
| 1 | Run M1 → M3 mutations to get every slot to 700 or more |
| 2 | Catacombs for 750 caches and Crowns: the easiest set source |
| 3 | Isle of Night once you're in the mid-700s. It drops up to 800 directly |
| 4 | Push to 800 with Umbrals ([[Gear Score to 800]]). The last 10 points cost the most, so do your weapon and main pieces first |

## Which set pieces to take

| Role | Take | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Tank | Tenacity (PvP track) first; Dreadwarden's heavy pieces for gear score | Second Wind only works while exhausted, which a blocking tank rarely is |
| Bruiser | Dreadwarden's (Isle of Night) or Tenacity | Both add lifesteal; Second Wind suits dodge-and-swing play |
| Melee DPS | Spectral Wrath (Isle of Night), Overcharged (Catacombs) | Damage stacks; Overcharged needs you to avoid being hit |
| Ranged DPS | Spectral Wrath | Enrage stacks build from hits within 13 m |
| Mage | Elementally Charged (Catacombs) | Stores your element for a non-magic weapon |
| Healer | Hallowed Aegis (Isle of Night) | Turns healing healthy allies into a big heal on a low one |

More per role: [[Gear Basics]].

# Hive of Gorgons

The first 10-player raid, in Cutlass Keys.⁠​‌‌​​​​​​‌​‌‌‌​‌‌‌‌‌‌​​‌⁠ It has three bosses with traps and Angry Earth mobs in between.

Related: [[1 Raids]] · [[Consumables]] · [[Gems]] · [[Artifacts]] · [[Gear Basics]]

## Getting in

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| Players | 10 (opens with 6) |
| Level | 65 |
| Gear score | As close to 725 as you can. Many groups farm the first boss to gear up |
| Entrance | South-east corner of Cutlass Keys, or the Activities tab |
| Enemy type | Angry Earth: bring Angry Earth ward potions and coatings. Slash and Fire damage are favoured |
| Lockout | Loot once per boss per week |
| Boss stats (game data) | 50% mitigation, Rend works at half strength, Weaken at about a third. Weak to Fire (+5%), Slash (+2.5%) and Thrust (+1%) |

## Suggested group

| Role | Count | Job |
|---|---|---|
| Tank | 1 | War Hammer for rend. Holds every mob and takes boss hits |
| Healers | 2 | One on the tank, one on the DPS |
| Spear DPS | 2 | Stack debuffs (one enfeeble, one bleed), Bow as the second weapon |
| Greatsword / Hatchet | 1 | Slash damage |
| Rapier | 2 | One evade, one bleed |
| Fire Staff | 2 | Ranged damage |

## 1. Echidna

| Mechanic | What to do |
|---|---|
| Arena | Big and vertical. Pillars rise during the fight |
| Pillars | Ranged DPS stand on top. Higher up means bonus damage and stamina damage, and less of her rock armour |
| Tank | Kite her around the outer rim |
| Obsidian Crystals | Claw-like crystals come out of the ground. DPS kill them at once. Missing the second wave can wipe the raid |
| Crystal launch | A crystal landing on you while you're on a pillar kills you. Dodge or jump off |
| Stamina break | When her stamina breaks she flips over. Everyone goes melee, applies rend and hits the upper middle of her body |
| Resistance | She deals mostly Strike damage: Onyx gems in armour |

**Debuffs from the game data**

| Debuff | Effect |
|---|---|
| Obsidian Weakness | Take 40% more damage while near an Obsidian Crystal |
| Rooted | Rooted until the Obsidian Missile is destroyed (up to 10 s) |
| Threat Detected (3 levels) | The lower you stand, the more of her rock armour soaks your hits |
| In the Clear | Bonus damage and stamina damage from pillar height |
| She's Exposed! | Bonus damage hitting her back after a stagger |

## 2. Typhon

| Mechanic | What to do |
|---|---|
| DPS check | Three phases. Each adds mobs and removes pillars. If the pillars run out before the next phase, you wipe |
| Weapons | Melee is fine here: spear, rapier or hatchet |
| Thorn lane | The left, middle or right lane glows red. Move out before the thorns come up |
| Targeted thorns | Red icon over your head: run to the edge away from the group and keep moving. More players get marked as his HP drops |
| Iron Maiden | Thorn cages trap players and hurt over time. Break them fast |
| Insta-charge | Instant kill. Hide behind a pillar |
| Corvids | Kill them fast or Typhon eats them for buffs. Gravity Well and Shockwave group them. Scorpion's Sting pulls them out of vines |
| Resistance | Nature: Nature protection amulet and Amber gems. Deal Slash or Nature |

**Debuffs from the game data**

| Debuff | Effect |
|---|---|
| Blighted Blood | Bleed 2% base health per second and take 15% more damage, 15 s |
| Painful Confinement | Thorn cage: 5% base Nature damage every 0.5 s, up to 12 s |
| Thorn Shackles | "Unless you found some cover, Typhon will execute you." 6 s. This is the charge: get behind a pillar |

## 3. Broodmother Medusa

| Mechanic | What to do |
|---|---|
| Difficulty | Easier than Typhon, with no DPS check |
| Eggs and flowers | Ranged DPS destroy them as they appear. Eggs that hatch spawn random mobs |
| Sleep powder | White powder puts you to sleep for up to 2 minutes unless someone cleanses you |
| Cleansing | Grab the glowing ball from a fountain on the outer rim and throw it to cleanse an area |
| Tank cleanser | One player keeps the tank's debuffs and DoTs down |
| Screech and charge | After a cleanse she screeches, picks a player and charges. Dodge it |
| Good DPS picks | Fire Staff, or Hatchet (it can be thrown, and Berserk helps you survive) |

**Debuffs from the game data**

| Debuff | Effect |
|---|---|
| Envenomed | 2.5% health per tick, 5 s |
| Medusa's Poison (pool) | 3% health per tick, 5 s |
| Gorgon's Gaze | 15% slow for 15 s |
| Petrifying | 50% of health and 50% slow over 8 s. Don't get caught by the gaze twice |

# Isle of Night

Season 10's 10-player raid, off the coast of Nighthaven.⁠​‌‌​​​​​​‌​‌‌‌​‌‌‌‌‌‌​​‌⁠ It has three bosses and is the only source of the Spectral Wrath, Dreadwarden's and Hallowed Aegis set pieces.

Related: [[1 Raids]] · [[Set Pieces]] · [[Gear Sets]] · [[Drop Limits]] · [[Gear Basics]]

> [!warning] Community guides for this raid are still thin, especially for Commander Thorpe. The **debuff tables** come straight from the game files, so they're reliable. The strategy notes are a summary of early guides: check them against your own group's calls.

## Getting in

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| Players | 10 (you can open it with 6 to practise) |
| Level | 70 |
| Gear score | Guides say aim for 780–800. One lists 650+ as the bare minimum |
| Unlock | Finish the Nighthaven story quests and the Season 10 intro missions |
| Entrance | Skull icon on Nighthaven's south coast. Nearest fast travel: Church of Grivaros. Or queue through Group Finder (Raids) |
| Lockout | One guide says there's no weekly loot cap. Not confirmed |
| Suggested group | 2 tanks, 2–3 healers, 5–6 DPS |
| Enemy type | **Lost** (game data): bring the Lost ward potion and Lost coating. Bosses have 50% mitigation, Rend works at half strength on them, and they're slightly weak to Nature (+5%), Strike (+2.5%) and Ice (+1.5%) |

## 1. Twin Jesters

| Mechanic | What to do |
|---|---|
| Overlapping AoEs and traps | Two bosses in one fight. Don't stand where both can hit you |
| Copies ("Find the real Jester") | The Jesters spawn decoys and everyone gets +40% move speed for 25 s. Spread out and find the real one |
| Add waves | Carcasses, woodcutters, villagers and a cryptkeeper join in. Tank picks them up |
| Trap lever (blue glow) | Assign one player. Pulling it slows the adds and damages them |
| Rewarding Audience | Players near the Jesters buff their attack and damage absorption. Only stand close if you need to |
| Positioning | No split needed. Stack near the tank so heals and cleaves land |

**Debuffs from the game data**

| Debuff | Effect |
|---|---|
| Pranked | 20% slow, take 20% more damage, deal 20% less damage, for 12 s |
| Burn (Hellring, Fiery Cackle trail, hits) | Fire damage over time, 1–5 s |
| Slow | 30% move speed reduction (3 s after explosions) |

## 2. Dahut and the Palatine Guards

| Mechanic | What to do |
|---|---|
| Four guards | Archer, Shieldbearer, Swordsman and Halberdier |
| Split | Group A (with a tank) pulls one guard away; group B damages another |
| 50% stasis | A guard goes inactive at 50% HP. Once all four are at 50% they come back. Then kill them one at a time |
| Dahut | Appears after the last guard. She's fast and drops fire and abyss areas on the floor |
| Guards return | In Dahut's phase, one tank holds Dahut and everyone else handles the guards |
| Abyss mark | Marked players are targeted by her Dance of Death. They counter "Abyss Instability", so marked players go to the guards |
| "Regroup with your allies!" | Stack up to share the damage |

**Debuffs from the game data**

| Debuff | Source | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| Palatine Rend | Swordsman | Take 10% more damage for 5 s |
| Disease | Shieldbearer (gong) | 50% less healing taken for 3 s |
| Decimate Jail | Halberdier | 2 s stun, then 5 s with no stamina regen |
| Palatine Smite | Halberdier | 30% slow for 2 s |
| Stranded Tether | Archer | Rooted for 2 s |
| Blazing Fission | Archer (ground) | 1% Fire damage per second per stack, 10 s |
| Standing in the abyss | Dahut | 30% slow and 83% less stamina regen while you stand in it |
| Abyssal Drain | Dahut (Purging Blade) | No stamina regen |

> [!tip] Tank note: the Halberdier's jail takes away your stamina regen. Don't be blocking on low stamina when it lands.

## 3. Commander Thorpe

The final boss. Guides call him the hardest fight in the game right now and haven't written up full strategies yet. Here's what the game data shows about his kit:

| Debuff | Effect | What it suggests |
|---|---|---|
| Spear Bearer | Holder keeps gaining Fragile Soul and pulls Thorpe's focus | A relic/spear that a player carries. Plan who holds it and rotate it |
| Fragile Soul | 4% base Fire damage every 1.2 s for 15 s | The cost of carrying the relic. Healers watch the carrier |
| Rooted (lost the relic) | Rooted for 6 s after losing the relic | Don't drop it carelessly |
| Mistlocked | Soul locked down: 3 s root | Impaling Mistlock: dodge the impale |
| Soul Exhaustion | Can't run or dodge for 4 s | Don't get caught near other hazards |
| Rend | Take 10% more damage for 20 s | Tank swap or a defensive cooldown if it stacks with other damage |

# Sandworm (Shah Neshen, the Devourer)

A 20-player Elite Trial in Brimstone Sands.⁠​‌‌​​​​​​‌​‌‌‌​‌‌‌‌‌‌​​‌⁠ It's one long fight with a big role split.

Related: [[1 Raids]] · [[Consumables]] · [[Heart Runes]] · [[Drop Limits]] · [[Gear Basics]]

## Getting in

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| Players | 20 (opens with 12) |
| Level / GS | 65, and groups usually want 690+ (the game suggests 600–625) |
| Entrance | Brimstone Sands. Activities tab → Elite Trial |
| Enemy type | The game data lists Shah Neshen as a **Beast** (70% physical and elemental mitigation, small Thrust weakness). Some guides say Angry Earth, but the data says Beast. The adds are Beasts too |
| Rewards limit | Daily box once per daily reset and weekly box once per week (from `LootLimits`: Trial_Sandworm_DailyBox / WeeklyBox) |

## Roles

| Role | Count | Job |
|---|---|---|
| Tank | 1 | Gathers adds (scorpions, mages) and holds the Sandworm in the stamina phase |
| Off-tank | 1 | Backup on adds |
| Healers | 2+ | AoE heals while adds are up |
| Lights | 4 | One per platform on the outer rim. They pick red or blue as the caller says |
| Caller | 1 | Stands below and calls the light colours, plus "Block!" |
| DPS | rest | Stack Rend (enfeeble spear, spear, S&S, War Hammer, Greatsword, Rapiers) |

## Phases

| Phase | What happens | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| Start | Hit the big drum | DPS stack on the left of the spawn |
| Adds | Scorpions and mages | Tank groups them. Ranged kill scorpions and mages first |
| Block call | The worm swings | Block when the caller says "Block!". Not blocking kills you |
| Lights | Colours appear under the four platform players; they can't see them | Caller calls them. All four right means a raid buff to shield stamina damage |
| Big shielded adds | Drop a sword when they die | Pick it up for Empower |
| Scorpion phase | Worm goes into its cave. One scorpion spawns on each side | Split left/right. Stay off glowing circles (it surfaces there). Avoid acid pools |
| Stairs | After both scorpions die | Tank, a healer, one DPS and two lights take the right stairs; everyone else goes left |
| Stamina phase | A sweep kills anyone slow on the stairs | Tank holds the worm; DPS swap to ranged; dodge acid spit when it faces you |
| Mine phase | Mines on the lower floor | Everyone except healers, lights and debuffers clears them |

## Debuffs and buffs from the game data

| Name | Effect |
|---|---|
| Acid Pool | 4% max health as Acid every 0.5 s, plus Acid affliction. Get out, or use an Acid tincture |
| Acid Storm | 1.5% max health as Acid every second |
| Digestive Juices | 2.5% max health as Acid every 0.5 s (where it devoured) |
| Acid Spew | 25% max health as Acid every second. Never stand in front of the spit |
| Poisoned (scorpions) | 4% base + 2% base health as Nature every 2 s for 20 s |
| Storm Chaser (buff) | Very resistant to Siege damage, and your melee hits apply 2% Rend (stacks to 25) |
| Shield Breaker (buff) | Bonus shield stamina damage. This is the lights reward |
| Shielded | The worm is immune to damage until the shield is broken |

> [!tip] Consumables: Beast ward and Beast coating for everyone (the worm and its adds are Beasts in the game data), an Acid tincture for pools, and a health potion.

## Rewards

| Box | Contents |
|---|---|
| Major Sandworm Spoils (weekly) | Dark Matter, Sandworm Materia, Minor Heartrune of the Devourer, Gypsum Orbs, chance at named gear |
| Minor Sandworm Spoils (daily) | Dark Matter, Sandworm Materia, Gypsum Orbs, chance at named gear |
| Notable | Sclerite Pincer (Great Axe). Tempest Fury artifact: kill the worm with it equipped to unlock its perk |

# Arenas (3v3)

Small, fast, on-demand PvP. Good practice for OPR and wars, and the best place to learn your build's matchups.

Related: [[1 PvP]] · [[PvP Reward Track]] · [[Season 10 PvP Changes]] · [[PvP Gear Rules]]

## Rules

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| Size | 3 v 3 |
| Level | 20+ |
| Queue | Modes menu, from anywhere. Solo queue puts you on a random team; queue as a group to keep your team |
| Match | Best of 5: first team to win 3 rounds |
| Length | About 10 minutes for a whole match (game data) |
| Round | 2 minutes, then a ring of fire closes in and pushes everyone to the middle |
| Late round | Incoming healing gets weaker the longer a round runs |
| Healers (S10) | Each team has either no healer or exactly one |
| Gear score | Scaled to 775 (S10) |
| Matchmaking | Cross-world and skill-based, with role selection |
| Maps | Hourly rotation since S8; Verdant Court (the big temple-grove map) joined in S9 |

## Rewards

| Reward | Detail |
|---|---|
| Every match | PvP XP and Azoth Salt; more rounds won means more reward |
| Daily | Up to 2 Garnet Gypsum, and an Arena cache (random weapon or armour) twice a day |

## Playing it as a tank

| Situation | Do |
|---|---|
| Team comp | You're the peel: stay near your healer or damage dealer, not the enemy's |
| Enemy healer | Lock them down when your damage dealer is ready to burst. Shield Bash, Vault Kick or Shockwave on cue |
| Fire ring closing | Healing is falling off, so trade cooldowns early rather than late |
| No healer on either side | Heavy armour and Stoneform win long rounds: play for attrition |
| Verdant Court | Bigger map with cover: ranged teams will try to kite you early, so use the walls |

Suggested builds: [[Spear Dive Assassin]], [[Shield Rush Bruiser]], [[Berserker Duelist]], [[Battle Healer]].

Short instanced matches added in Season 9. Grab the enemy flag and carry it home while your own flag is still at base.

Related: [[1 PvP]] · [[PvP Reward Track]] · [[Season 10 PvP Changes]]

## Rules

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| Size | 10 v 10, level 60 (game data) |
| Length | About 15 minutes |
| Score | Bring the enemy flag to your base **while your flag is home** |
| Win | Most points when time runs out |
| Maps | Frozen Pass and Forbidden City, 50/50 rotation |
| Power-ups | On the map: Damage (30s Empower), Heal (flat 10,000 health), Speed (7s Haste) |
| Healers (S10) | At least one per team; teams differ by one at most |
| Gear score | Scaled to 775 (S10) |
| Neutral flag (S10 event) | A middle flag spawns a few minutes in; either team can score it, worth less than an enemy flag |

| Reward | Detail |

| Role | Job | Fits |

# Duels

Free, no-risk PvP against anyone who accepts.⁠​‌‌​​​​​​‌​‌‌‌​‌‌‌‌‌‌​​‌⁠ The best way to learn matchups and test a build before taking it to OPR or arenas.

Related: [[1 PvP]] · [[Arenas (3v3)]] · [[Open World PvP]]

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| Level | 10+ (no faction or PvP flag needed) |
| Start one | Look at the player, press **H**, then **Duel Player**; or type `/duel playername` |
| Where | Anywhere outside settlements; not during a war or invasion |
| Group duels | Form a group first, then pick **Duel Group**. Up to 5 a side, and sides don't have to be even (1v2, 2v3...) |
| Interference | Anyone else joining in ends it as a draw |
| Cost | Nothing: no durability loss, no death penalty |

| Stun chains | Count your Shield Bash / Shockwave / Vault Kick timings against a dodger |
| Point tanking | 1v2 or 1v3 duel to see how long you survive with Stoneform |

# Wars

Wars are the 50v50 territory sieges.⁠​‌‌​​​​​​‌​‌‌‌​‌‌‌‌‌‌​​‌⁠ A company fights for control of a settlement; the winner governs it and collects the taxes.

| Note | What's in it |
|---|---|
| [[War Roles]] | The five roles, what each one does, and how to split 50 players |
| [[War Builds]] | A build per role, with gear, perks, gems and heart runes |
| [[Siege Weapons & Supplies]] | Every attacker and defender siege weapon, traps, and what Battle Tokens buy |
| [[War Prep Checklist]] | What to sort before you sign up |

Related: [[1 PvP]] · [[Tank PvP Playstyle]] · [[1 Builds]] · [[PvP Gear Tier List]] · [[New World Home]]

> [!warning] **Gear score is not scaled in Wars.** Unlike OPR, Arena and CTF (all scaled to 775), Wars use your real gear score. Get to 800 first — see [[Gear Score to 800]].

## How a war happens

| Step | Detail |
|---|---|
| 1. Influence | Companies push a territory into a **State of Conflict** by doing faction PvP missions there, which fills their faction's influence bar |
| 2. Declaration | Once the bar is full, war is declared at the territory's **Fort** |
| 3. First declarer | The company with the most influence gets the first **10 minutes** to declare, and must bid **5,000**, **10,000** or **15,000** gold |
| 4. Other bids | Any company that contributed at least **10%** to the State of Conflict can also bid |
| 5. Governing company | A higher bid improves your odds of being picked (it's still random). The winner is the **Vanguard**: it manages the 50-man roster and, if it wins, owns the territory and its taxes |
| 6. Window | The **defending** company sets the time the war runs |
| 7. Sign-up | Sign up at the **War Board** in any settlement. The company leader picks the roster, and generally picks level 60+ players |
| 8. Invite | Selected players get the invite **15 minutes** before the war and are teleported straight in at the start |

## The battle

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| Size | 50 v 50 |
| Length | About **30 minutes**, shorter if the attackers steamroll it |
| Objectives | Capture or defend **three control points (A, B, C)**, then the **Fort** |
| Attacker route | Take the three **Rally Points** in front of the Fort before you can damage or breach the Fort gates |
| Rally points | They're respawn points and give Armory access. Once the attackers take one, defenders **can't take it back** |
| Capturing | You need **more players on the point** than the other side for it to start flipping |
| Defender spawns | After the attackers push in, defenders pick a spawn inside the Fort. There are several Fort entrances to cover |
| Repairs | Defenders get Siege Supplies from **Siege Supply Generators** |
| Scoreboard | Press **N** |
| Currency | You earn **Battle Tokens** during the war and spend them at the Armory (see [[Siege Weapons & Supplies]]) |
| Who's favoured | **Defenders.** Attackers need a real plan |

## After it ends

| Result | What happens |
|---|---|
| Defenders hold | They keep the territory |
| Attackers win | A new settlement government forms with the Vanguard as the governing company |
| Either way | A post-match stats screen, then you return to a settlement |
| Rewards | Azoth, gold, standing and an item box of random gear, win or lose. Wars are also a good Umbral source |

## Tips

| Tip | Why |
|---|---|
| Have a plan, then change it | No one strategy works everywhere. Adjusting mid-fight keeps the enemy guessing |
| Spread across points | Splitting your forces can confuse the enemy about where the real push is |
| Keep morale up | Teams that lose faith and wander aimlessly almost always lose, and fights do swing back |
| Don't skimp on healers | Too few healers is the usual reason a point fight is lost |
| Kill the siege crews | A ranged player picking people off cannons is worth more than their damage numbers suggest |

| Weapon | What it does | Best against |

| Weapon | What it does | Best against |
|---|---|---|

# War Prep Checklist

Related: [[1 Wars]] · [[War Builds]] · [[Gear Grind]] · [[Gear Score to 800]]

## Before the war

| # | Do this | Why |
|---|---|---|

| 3 | Match your gems to your attunement | Avoid Fire and Ice, which most players resist. See [[Gems]] |
| 4 | Pick a heart rune and know what it's for | Stoneform to survive a choke, Detonate for damage into clumps. Play safe after using Detonate |

| 6 | Stock food and potions from your own bags | Battle Tokens only start coming in once the war is running |
| 7 | Join the voice channel | A roster that can't hear a call-out loses points it should hold |

# War Roles

A war roster needs a spread of all five roles.⁠​‌‌​​​​​​‌​‌‌‌​‌‌‌‌‌‌​​‌⁠ Builds for each are in [[War Builds]].

Related: [[1 Wars]] · [[War Builds]] · [[Tank PvP Playstyle]]

## The five roles

| Role | Job | Typical weapons |
|---|---|---|
| **Tank** | Hold points, keep the capture count in your favour, cut the damage your allies take, apply CC | Sword & Shield + War Hammer (heavy) |
| **Healer** | Keep the roster alive. Essential to winning point fights | Life Staff + Rapier or Void Gauntlet |
| **Melee / bruiser** | The core of any point fight. Soak spell damage, cleave, and win points through sheer numbers | Great Axe + War Hammer |
| **Ranged** | Pick off named targets and siege weapon crews from a distance | Musket (+ Bow or Hatchet) |
| **Caster** | Mass AoE damage and CC onto a packed control point | Ice Gauntlet + Void Gauntlet, or Fire Staff |

> [!tip] Crowd control, not raw damage, is what secures kills in a war. Dedicated CC players (War Hammer bruisers, Ice Gauntlet casters) matter more than extra damage dealers.

## Splitting 50 players

One example split from the Icy Veins guide:

| Point | Players | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| B (middle) | **30** | The main fight. Most of your tanks, healers and melee |
| A | **10** | Enough to contest and hold |
| C | **10** | Same |

Each of those groups needs its own tanks, healers and damage. A group of 10 with no healer loses its point.

## Where you fit as a tank

| Option | What it looks like |
|---|---|
| Point tank (heavy) | Stand on the circle, block, chain CC with the hammer, lean on your healer. Full detail in [[Tank PvP Playstyle]] |
| Dive bruiser (light) | Jump the backline and lock down healers and priority targets |
| Gate tank (attacking) | Soak the Fire Dropper and gate damage while the Powder Keg is lit |

# Builds

# Gear Basics

The rules every build follows, then one page per role with the artifacts, perks, gems and attribute splits that role's builds share.⁠​‌‌​​​​​​‌​‌‌‌​‌‌‌‌‌‌​​‌⁠ Each role page is taken from the Full loadout tables of that role's builds, so it matches what the loadout builder loads.

Related: [[1 Builds]] · [[Set Pieces]] · [[Gear Sets]] · [[Artifacts]] · [[Perk Dictionary]] · [[PvP Gear Rules]]

## Pick your role

| Role | Page | Armour | Main attributes | Builds that use it |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Tank | [[Tank Gear Basics]] | Heavy | Strength + Constitution | Immovable Juggernaut, Hybrid Control Tank, Shield Bash Tank, Frontline Hybrid, Solo Sustain Tank |
| Bruiser | [[Bruiser Gear Basics]] | Heavy or medium | Strength + Constitution | Open-World Bruiser, Melee Bruiser, Shield Rush Bruiser, War Hammer Dive Bruiser, Spear Dive Assassin |
| Melee DPS | [[Melee DPS Gear Basics]] | Light | Dexterity or Strength | Bleed Rapier, Berserker Duelist, AoE Cleaver |
| Ranged DPS | [[Ranged DPS Gear Basics]] | Light | Dexterity | Long-Range Specialist, Skirmisher, Toxic Arrow, Assassin, Siege Sniper, Hybrid Burst |
| Mage | [[Mage Gear Basics]] | Light | Intelligence | Frost Mage, Glass Cannon, Support Mage, AoE Specialist |
| Healer | [[Healer Gear Basics]] | Light (medium chest) | Focus + Constitution | Hybrid Support Healer, Battle Healer, Group Healer |

## Rules for every build

| Rule | Detail |
|---|---|
| One artifact of each kind | One weapon, one armour and one jewellery artifact at a time |
| Enchanted Ward everywhere | Every role's armour runs Enchanted Ward on as many pieces as possible |
| Wards in the gem slots | Physical Ward IV and Elemental Ward IV on armour (more Physical for PvP and melee content, more Elemental for magic-heavy bosses) |
| Refreshing | Cooldown reduction. Four at most across your gear |
| Freedom | Counts in stacks: run 3 or 5, never 1 or 2 |
| Shirking Heals | PvP only. Each piece stacks, so builds run it on all five armour charms |
| Jewellery | No attributes in Season 10. Pick it for its perks |
| Gear score | Everything can go to 800 with Umbral Crystals. See [[Gear Score to 800]] |

## PvE or PvP: what changes

| Slot | PvE builds | PvP builds |
|---|---|---|
| Third armour perk | Elemental Aversion, Health, Refreshing | Shirking Energy |
| Armour charms | Vicious, Keen, Keenly Empowered (damage) or Freedom (tanks) | Shirking Heals or Freedom |
| Weapon perks | Keenly Jagged + Keenly Empowered + Enchanted, or a named weapon | The same, with more named and artifact weapons |
| Consumables | Ward potions and coatings for the enemy type. See [[Consumables]] | Absorption potions, attribute food |

| Slot | Artifact | What it does |

| Amulet | **Lost Stopwatch** (Mutated Depths) | +300% threat |

> [!important] You can wear **one weapon artifact, one armour artifact and one jewellery artifact** at a time. So it's Void Darkplate **or** The Unmoved, and Lost Stopwatch **or** Blooddrinker. Each build's Full loadout table picks one of each.

> [!warning] Some guides list **Odo** as the tank amulet. Odo is a **flail** artifact. The tank amulet is Lost Stopwatch. The Unmoved is **boots**, not a chest piece.

# Hit-and-Run Leveler — Hatchet + Bow

The easy one.⁠​‌‌​​​​​​‌​‌‌‌​‌‌‌‌‌‌​​‌⁠ Open at range, finish in melee, self-heal through everything. Good for levelling an alt or mixed PvE/PvP roaming.

| Modes | [[Open World Activities\|Open-world PvE]] |
| Armor | Light for mobility. Go heavier if you keep dying |
| Attributes | 100 Strength / 350 Dexterity / 50 Constitution |
| Difficulty | Easy |
| Strengths | Self-healing, handles groups, ranged opener, works in PvE and PvP |
| Weakness | Squishy in light armor |

## Gear

| Slot | Pick |
|---|---|

| Armor | Light for mobility |
| Jewelry | Crit and damage perks (no attributes in S10) |

## Abilities

| Bow | **Penetrating Shot** | Opener; pierces several targets |
| Bow | **Rapid Shot** | Sustained damage |
| Bow | **Rain of Arrows** | Ground AoE for packs |
| Hatchet | **Berserk** | Self-heal, speed and damage |
| Hatchet | **Rending Throw** | Your main Rend, single target |

## Passives

| Bow | Skirmisher | **Mark**, Archer's Speed | – |
| Hatchet | Berserker | **Enraged Strikes**, **Fortifying Strikes**, Frenzied Purge | **Defy Death** |

> [!note] Some guides list this build with translated or outdated ability names (Piercing Shot, Quick Shot, Arrow Barrage, Tearing Throw). The names above are the ones in the game data.

## How to play it

Open with Penetrating Shot at max range, Rain of Arrows if there are several, then swap to the Hatchet when they reach you. Berserk is both your heal and your damage window. Rejuvenating Crits keeps you topped up between fights so you don't burn potions.

# Shield Lancer — Sword & Shield + Spear

> [!warning] **Not from a guide.** No Season 10 guide has an open-world build for this pair — S&S + Spear only appears as a PvP dive build ([[Spear Dive Assassin]]). This is put together from the two weapons' own ability and skill-tree guides, so treat it as a starting point rather than a tested build.

Two crowd-control weapons on one bar.⁠​‌‌​​​​​​‌​‌‌‌​‌‌‌‌‌‌​​‌⁠ You stun-lock packs instead of out-damaging them, and the Spear's best passive rewards you for it.

Why the pair works: Sword & Shield scales mainly off **Strength** (Dexterity second) and the Spear mainly off **Dexterity** (Strength second), so a Str/Dex split raises both.

Related: [[1 Builds]] · [[Bruiser Gear Basics]] · [[Shield Ranger]] · [[Spear Dive Assassin]] · [[Skill Trees]]

| Role | Solo bruiser / CC |
| Modes | [[Open World Activities\|Open-world PvE]] |
| Armor | Medium (heavy chest if you keep dying) |
| Attributes | 250 Strength / 150 Dexterity / 100 Constitution |
| Best for | Solo elites, mob packs, flagged PvP |

| Weakness | Less AoE than Great Axe or Hammer, and CC-immune bosses blunt the whole plan |

# Shield Bash Tank — Sword & Shield + Hatchet

The forgiving starter tank.⁠​‌‌​​​​​​‌​‌‌‌​‌‌‌‌‌‌​​‌⁠ Good threat and heavy cooldown reduction, and the Hatchet gives you a self-heal and a get-out-of-death card while you learn.

| Modes | [[Expeditions Overview\|Expeditions & raids]] |
| Armor | Not specified in the guide — heavy is the safe choice |
| Attributes | 275 Strength / 225 Constitution |
| Best for | Solo play and group PvE while you're learning to tank |
| Strengths | Very forgiving; good threat generation and cooldown reduction |
| Weakness | The Hatchet contributes almost nothing to actual tanking |

## Weapons

| Sword | Strength | **Taunting IV** — essential, it's what makes Shield Bash taunt | Fortifying Shield Rush |
| Shield | Strength or Con | – | Tower Shield |
| Hatchet | Strength | Any | Ability choice is up to you |

| Artifacts | Blooddrinker ring is the big one; add Void Darkplate and The Unmoved when you get them |
| Heart rune | Stalwart Stoneform |

## Abilities

| Weapon | Ability | Why |
|---|---|---|
| S&S | **Upheaval** | Your damage, and it cuts other cooldowns |
| S&S | **Shield Bash** | Fast stun, and a 6s taunt on everything hit with the taunt gem (Taunting IV) equipped |
| S&S | **Defender's Resolve** | Damage reduction and an AoE taunt |
| Hatchet | Berserk, Feral Rush, Social Distancing | Self-heal, gap close, escape — pick what you like |

## Passives

| S&S | Defender | **Sturdy Shield**, **Defensive Training**, High Grip (ranged block), One with the Shield, **Recuperation** | **Defensive Formation** |
| S&S | Swordmaster | **Counter Attack** (threat) | – |

## How to play it

| Step | Do |
|---|---|
| 1 | Open with Shield Bash to taunt and stun the pack |
| 2 | Defender's Resolve when the damage starts landing — it also drains the attacker's stamina |
| 3 | Upheaval whenever it's up, to pull your other cooldowns forward |
| 4 | Block between abilities. One with the Shield turns blocking into cooldown reduction |
| 5 | Swap to Hatchet and Berserk if you're low and the healer is busy |

Once you're comfortable, [[Immovable Juggernaut]] does everything this does but better, because the War Hammer actually adds mitigation and CC.

# AoE Specialist — Bow + Void Gauntlet

**Rated 4★ PvP / 5★ PvE.** Arguably the highest damage into a big clump of players, which makes it an OPR and war pick rather than a duelling build. Low defences, so it lives or dies on positioning.

| Void Gauntlet | **Oblivion** | A circle that damages over time, empowers you and allies, and can strip enemy buffs |

Oblivion onto the contested point for the ally Empower and the buff strip, Orb of Decay through the clump, then bow damage from the back.⁠​‌‌​​​​​​‌​‌‌‌​‌‌‌‌‌‌​​‌⁠ Petrifying Scream when anyone reaches you. Voidcaller is a group cooldown, not a personal one — drop it where your melee are standing.

**Rated 4★ PvP / 4★ PvE.** Ranged pressure with enough spear crowd control to peel anyone who closes on you. Easier than [[Skirmisher]] because the Spear gives you three ways to stop a melee player instead of relying on dodges.

# Hybrid Burst — Blunderbuss + Musket

**Rated 4★ PvP / 4★ PvE.** Explosive Intelligence-scaled burst at close range, with the Musket for anything far away. Built around the 350 Intelligence breakpoint.

Related: [[1 Builds]] · [[Ranged DPS Gear Basics]] · [[PvP Gear Rules]] · [[Siege Sniper]] · [[Inferno Blaster]] · [[Skill Trees]]

# PvP Gear Rules

Rules that apply to every PvP build, so the build files don't repeat them.

Related: [[1 Builds]] · [[Gems]] · [[Perk Dictionary]] · [[Heart Runes]] · [[PvP Gear Tier List]]

## Gems and perks

| Item | Rule |
|---|---|
| Elemental gem / runeglass | Match your **Attunement** (or Chain) perk to its element. **Avoid Fire and Ice** — most players resist them |
| Punishing Runeglass | 1-3 pieces at most, never all 5. It has an internal cooldown, so extra copies do nothing |
| Refreshing | No more than 4 Refreshing perks in total |
| Armor third perk | Elemental Aversion, Freedom, Health or Slash Conditioning |
| Stacking perks | Freedom and Shirking Heals count in stacks across 5 pieces. Run 3 or 5, never 1 or 2 |

## Attributes

| Item | Rule |
|---|---|
| 150 Constitution | Reduces the crit damage you take. The standard floor for light builds |
| 200 Constitution | The baseline for most PvP, and for anything that holds a point |
| Jewelry | **No attributes in Season 10.** Pick jewelry for perks only |

## Heart runes

| Pick | When |
|---|---|
| Stalwart / Cunning **Stoneform** | Defensive, breaks CC chains. The safe default |
| Brutal **Detonate** | Burst into clumps. Play safe after using it |
| Stalwart **Dark Ascent** | An invulnerable attack that heals you — good for squishy casters |

Full list in [[Heart Runes]].

## Armor weight

| Weight | Effect |
|---|---|
| Light | +20% damage, full dodge roll. Dies to focus fire |
| Medium | The usual compromise. Most builds run a medium chest with light everything else |
| Heavy | ~15% better blocking, CC you apply lasts ~20% longer, highest armor. No roll, and you need a healer |

-# Tank PvP Playstyle

Related: [[1 Builds]] · [[1 Wars]] · [[War Roles]] · [[Outpost Rush]] · [[Team Score]]

> [!note] Gathered from community guides (Icy Veins etc.). The meta is still Season 10 (Nighthaven), which now runs until the servers close on 31 Jan 2027.

## Two ways to play Sword & Shield in PvP

| | Point / frontline tank | Dive bruiser |
|---|---|---|
| Job | Sit on capture points, keep your numbers up, soak damage, CC enemies on the point | Jump the backline and lock down one target (healers, priority targets) until it dies |
| Weapons | Sword & Shield + War Hammer | Sword & Shield + War Hammer |
| Armor | Heavy | Light (all pieces) |
| Attributes | ~300 Str / 200 Con | Pure Str, 100–200 Con |
| Sword abilities | Leaping Strike (instead of Upheaval for PvP), Shield Rush, Defender's Resolve / Shield Bash | Leaping Strike, Shield Bash, Shield Rush (or Upheaval) |
| Hammer abilities | Shockwave, Clear Out / Armor Breaker, Path of Destiny | Wrecking Ball, Shockwave, Path of Destiny |
| Needs | A healer behind you | Good timing on the opener |
| Best in | Wars, OPR outposts | OPR skirmishes, small fights |

## Passives

> [!info] Passive picks are suggestions put together from Icy Veins' skill-tree ratings ("always take" nodes and best ultimates), because the build guides only show passives as images. You get ~19 points per weapon at mastery 20, so take the listed ones first and spend leftovers on filler. One ultimate per weapon. Names and tree placement checked against the game data; full trees in [[Skill Trees]], ability perks in [[Perk Charms]].

| Style | Weapon | Key passives | Ultimate |
|---|---|---|---|
| Point tank | Sword & Shield | Defender: **Sturdy Shield** (+15% physical armor), **Defensive Training** (20% Fortify for 5s on block), High Grip (ranged block), One with the Shield, **Recuperation** (+10% incoming healing); Swordmaster: **Invigorating Bulwark** (PvP) | **Defensive Formation** (30% less damage to allies within 4m while blocking) |
| Point tank | War Hammer | Crowd Crusher: **Outnumbered**, **Prevailing Spirit** (heals from Shockwave / Path of Destiny), Concussive Impact; Juggernaut: **Hardened Steel** (Grit + 12% DR), Quick Recovery | **Aftershock** (abilities slow) |
| Dive bruiser | Sword & Shield | Swordmaster: **Opportunist** (abilities deal +10% to *slowed* foes — Shield Rush slows), **Precision**, **Critical Precision** (haste), Confidence, Mobility | **Leadership** (party +10% dmg) or Defender's **Defensive Formation** for safety |
| Dive bruiser | War Hammer | Crowd Crusher: **Prevailing Spirit** (heals off Path of Destiny / Shockwave), **Concussive Impact**, Outnumbered; Juggernaut: Hardened Steel | **Aftershock** (abilities slow) |

## Why heavy armor for point tanking

| Heavy armor bonus | Effect |
|---|---|
| Blocking | ~15% more |
| CC you apply | ~20% longer duration |
| Armor values | Highest |
| Downside | Short dodge, slow; you depend on healers |

## How a point tank plays

| Situation | What to do |
|---|---|
| Your team is on a point | Stand **on** the circle. Bodies on the point win captures, so staying alive matters more than kills |
| Enemy melee clumps on the point | Shield Rush (AoE slow + stagger) → swap → Shockwave (AoE stun) |
| Enemy healer keeps them alive | Path of Destiny to interrupt, or Leaping Strike in and Shield Bash (fast stun) |
| Taking burst damage | Block. With Defensive Formation, blocking also cuts damage to allies within 4m by 30% |
| Low on health | Back toward your healer. Don't chase off the point |
| Enemy tank in the way | Armor Breaker (armor penetration) is the tank-vs-tank tool |
| Wrecking Ball | Gives Fortify, so use it to engage safely as well as for the knockdown |
| Heart rune | Stalwart Stoneform for choke points and self-sustain; Detonate for damage vs clumps (play safe after using it) |

## Dive bruiser combos (lock one target down)

| Step | Shield Rush version | Upheaval version | Hammer opener |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Leaping Strike from behind | Leaping Strike from behind | Wrecking Ball |
| 2 | Shield Rush | Shield Bash (stun) | Shockwave |
| 3 | Shield Bash (stun) | Upheaval | Swap → Leaping Strike |
| 4 | Swap → Wrecking Ball | Swap → Wrecking Ball | Shield Rush (Shield Bash if using Upheaval) |
| 5 | Shockwave | Shockwave | Shield Bash (Upheaval if taken) |
| 6 | Hammer heavy/light attack | Hammer heavy/light attack | Heavy attack from behind |

> [!tip] Everything depends on landing the opener. If Leaping Strike or Wrecking Ball misses, back off and wait for the cooldown.

## Dive bruiser perks

| Item | Pick |
|---|---|
| Damage perks | Empowering Leaping Strike, Sundering Shockwave, Penetrating Wrecking Ball |
| Defensive perks | Fortifying Shield Rush, Leeching Path of Destiny |
| Gems | Match Attunement/Chain perks to your Opal's element |

## Outpost Rush tips for tanks

| Tip | Why |
|---|---|
| Anchor an outpost instead of roaming | Each held outpost = 1 team point every 3 s (see [[Team Score]]) |
| Contest the capture circle | 0.05 personal pts per tick; a full capture = 90 (see [[Personal Contribution Points]]) |
| Assists count as much as kills | Assist = 50 pts. CC that sets up kills scores well |
| Stick with a healer | Heavy builds need healer support to work in PvP |

## Ability perks explained

Ability perks named above, with their Season 10 effect from the game data (base value; scales with gear score). More in [[Perk Charms]].

| Perk | Effect |
|---|---|
| Empowering Leaping Strike | All attacks deal +13% damage to targets Slowed by Leaping Strike's Cowardly Punishment upgrade. |
| Fortifying Shield Rush | After hitting a target with Shield Rush, gain Fortify, increasing armor by 15% for 6s. |
| Leeching Path of Destiny | Heal for 7% of the damage dealt by Path Of Destiny. |
| Penetrating Wrecking Ball | Wrecking Ball penetrates 18% of the target's armor. |
| Sundering Shockwave | Shockwave inflicts Rend, reducing the target's armor by 8% for 8s. |

# Toxic Arrow — Bow + Hatchet

**Rated 4★ PvP / 4★ PvE.** Damage-over-time pressure instead of burst, with two ways out of crowd control and Defy Death as a safety net. The most survivable of the bow builds.

Related: [[1 Builds]] · [[Ranged DPS Gear Basics]] · [[PvP Gear Rules]] · [[Skirmisher]] · [[Assassin]] · [[Hit-and-Run Leveler]]

| Difficulty | Medium |
| Strengths | Strong DoT damage, two CC escapes, and Defy Death |
| Weakness | Much less burst than [[Skirmisher]] |

# Group Healer — Life Staff + Rapier

The most important build to learn if you ever heal a war.⁠​‌‌​​​​​​‌​‌‌‌​‌‌‌‌‌‌​​‌⁠ It exists to keep a 5-man team fighting, **not** to top the healing scoreboard. Too few healers is the usual reason a point fight is lost.

Related: [[1 Builds]] · [[Healer Gear Basics]] · [[1 Wars]] · [[War Roles]] · [[Heart Runes]] · [[Skill Trees]]

> [!warning] This guide was last updated in **October 2023 for Season One**, so its Fortify values and some perks predate Season 10's perk redesign. Verify in-game.

## Quick reference

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| Role | Healer |
| Modes | [[1 Wars\|Wars]] |
| Armor | Light, with a **medium chest** |
| Attributes | 300 Focus / 200 Constitution |
| Best for | Wars, and any organised 5-man PvP group |

## Gear

| Slot | Weight | Gem | Attribute |
|---|---|---|---|
| Life Staff | – | Cut Pristine Diamond | Focus |
| Rapier | – | Cut Pristine Amber | Focus |
| Helmet | Light | Cut Pristine Opal | Focus or Con |
| Chest | **Medium** | Cut Pristine Opal | Focus or Con |
| Gloves | Light | Cut Pristine Opal | Focus or Con |
| Pants | Light | Cut Pristine Opal | Focus or Con |
| Boots | Light | Cut Pristine Onyx | Focus or Con |
| Amulet / Ring / Earring | – | Cut Pristine Onyx | No attributes (S10) |

Best Life Staff: **Glowing Lifecrystal Staff** from mutated Dynasty Shipyard, or craft one with Materia. Most armor pieces are crafted or BoE.

## Perks

| Perk | Rule |
|---|---|
| Freedom | 5 stacks ideally. At fewer, 3 stacks plus other perks is preferred |
| Refreshing | **Always 5 stacks.** Put it on jewelry if a gear slot is too expensive |
| Ability perks | Anywhere they fit. Watch **Fortifying Sacred Ground** — it interacts badly with Invigorated Punishment, and Fortify was nerfed |

## Heart rune

|---|---|

| Minor Stoneform | The most defensive: break CC, immune to stagger, defensive buffs |

## Abilities

|---|---|
| **Divine Embrace** | Cast burst heal on a party member. AoE potential through Shared Struggle and Rebound |
| **Sacred Ground** | Zone at a target's feet: burst plus heal over time, and it amplifies healing received through Anointed |
| **Beacon** | Aimed projectile that sticks to the first player or surface it hits. **Put it on front-line melee** so the healing zone moves with the fight. Drop it on the ground during heavy damage |
| Orb of Protection (alt) | Burst plus heal over time, 10% Fortify, and Mending Protection |
| Light attack | Filler that heals through Blissful Touch |
| Rapier | **Riposte** (stun and block an incoming attack), **Evade** (dodge abilities, brief invulnerability, haste and stamina back), **Fleche** (long dash to escape or reposition) |
| Void Gauntlet (alt secondary) | More healing output, at the cost of the Rapier's mobility |

## Rotation

|---|---|
| 1 | Dodge, to get Bend Light |
| 2 | Orb of Protection for Mending Protection, Fortify and the heal over time |
| 3 | Sacred Ground on your target, to raise the healing they receive |
| 4 | Beacon on the melee clump, or for extra AoE healing |
| 5 | Divine Embrace on anyone losing big chunks of health |
| 6 | Light attacks as filler while cooldowns come back |

## Playing it in a war

|---|---|
| Focus | Mobility, positioning and cooldown management. You dive in and out to keep the team up |
| Beacon | Always on the front-line melee, so healing follows the fight |
| Rapier | Your escape. Fleche out, don't try to tank |
| Mindset | Empower your 5-man team. Personal healing numbers are not the goal |

# Siege Sniper — Musket + Bow or Hatchet

The ranged war slot.⁠​‌‌​​​​​​‌​‌‌‌​‌‌‌‌‌‌​​‌⁠ Its real value isn't its damage board position — it's deleting people off cannons and turrets, which no other role does well. Rated a top-tier war spec for ranged groups, especially on the **defending** team.

| Attributes | 350 Dexterity / 50 Intelligence / 100 Constitution |

## How to play it

| Situation | Do |
|---|---|
| Enemy stacked on a point | Ice Shower, then Ice Storm on top |
| Your melee pushing in | Oblivion on them for the Empower, and to strip the enemy's buffs |
| Enemy healer keeping them up | Orb of Decay through the clump; Disintegrate plus your team's damage |
| Someone reaches you | Petrifying Scream, then Entombed if that fails |
| Big group fight on a gate | Voidcaller where your melee are standing — it heals them while it damages the enemy |

There's also a **light-armor burst variant** (Ice Spikes, or Fire Staff + Ice Gauntlet) with room in war rosters, but that's a kill-squad role rather than support. See [[Glass Cannon]] for the fire version.
